ground_truth: I hate that the federal government has to get involved in this. We've stayed out of it, or I have. You know, I know quite a bit about it, obviously. The Commerce Committee, who is oversight for this, obviously has been involved. I'm on the Education Committee, which we have not really had a lot of discussions on because we've left it to the Commerce. A lot of people try to get involved. Yes, I've talked to committees in the NCAA. I've talked to coaches. I've talked to players, former players. I've talked to commissioners, athletic directors. And I was hoping that they could come up with something, but you can't get a consensus. You know, everybody wants it their way, and it's not possible. So I sat down with my staff. We talked about it, you know, the direction we would go. You can't do anything here in Washington, D.C., unless you have a bipartisan approach. It's not going to happen. Joe Manchin has got a lot of power up here. He's on the Democratic side. He and I sat down one day, and we got together, and we both came to the conclusion we've got to do something. We've got to help. He thinks that he can deliver people on the left. I hopefully can deliver people on the right, try to get this done. Now, we're not into the money part, you know, we're not trying to limit what people can do. What we want to do, at the end of the day, is come up with some standards and rules for all 50 states. That's what we can do in the federal government. We can pass a bill, and it takes 60 votes to pass a bill, then it'd have to go to the House, that all 50 states have to go by these guidelines. Right now, there is no guidelines. It is a... It's a disaster, just listening to coaches, and what's going on, and parents and players, you know, getting involved, which, fine, but at the end of the day, we want it fair for everybody in 50 states, and we want to make sure that we look out for two things, the student-athlete and their education. Those two have to be involved. So, we're not here to invent a wheel. Again, we're going to do our due diligence. Joe Manchin and I sent out a letter to a lot of people last few weeks, all over the country. Some people are saying, well, this is just the SEC deal. No, it's not. I don't know where they got that from, but this is a proposal that we will possibly put into law that can help and guideline everybody in all 50 states in this country. And at the end of the day, I hope we can do it. We might not be able to pull this off.
